output.summary: A leafy green annual, rarely biennial, native to Central and Western Asia. It has variable oval-to-triangular leaves and small green, wind-pollinated flowers, usually borne on separate male and female plants. Its leaves are commonly eaten fresh, cooked or preserved.
output.edibilityNote: Leaves are eaten fresh or cooked and may be canned, frozen or dehydrated; blanching can reduce oxalates.
